mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant for two consecutive months above 5.0%, market expectations for future rate cuts increase, lowering real discount rates and boosting equity present-value pricing, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: FOMC holds or signals hold after a restrictive stance
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day average during similar non-tightening windows (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% month-over-month and UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points in the same month
regime_hint: Labor market strengthening with low inflation
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative during 30 such labor-market events in a 2-year window (cumulative t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in retail sales (HOUST) exceeding 2% for three consecutive months predicts a near-term boost in consumer spending, which elevates earnings growth expectations and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >2% month-over-month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive during 10 such demand spikes (bootstrap p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 0.5% for two consecutive months indicates weakening supply-side constraints, prompting market participants to price in higher future demand and equity valuations, which results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative during 15 such contractions in a 12-month period (median vs. mean t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When core inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 237 for two consecutive months, the Fed is likely to maintain a higher policy rate for longer, which increases discount rates and compresses equity present value, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day average during similar inflation spikes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in job openings (RSAFS) below 7 million coinciding with a rise in layoffs (PAYEMS) suggests a softening labor market, lowering consumer and business confidence and pushing S&P 500 forward returns to negative over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 7,000,000 and PAYEMS falls by >5% month-over-month in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns remain positive during 10 such labor-market softening events (bootstrap p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in consumer confidence (not directly observable in the catalog) is proxied by a 3-month consecutive decline in retail sales (HOUST) below 450, which predicts a near-term risk-off move and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative during 20 such declines (bootstrap p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 102 over two consecutive months, without a corresponding increase in employment (PAYEMS), signals excess supply and a potential equity valuation correction, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 102 and PAYEMS flat or falling for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative during 15 such supply shocks (median vs. mean t-test p < 0.05).
